# Draft:Timeline of Kathiri

This timeline of the Kathiri states covers the period from 1395 to 30 November 1967.
First Kathiri Sultanate (1395–c. 1730)
The First Kathiri Sultanate, often referred to as the "Greater Kathiri" state, was established as a regional power with maritime dominance and territorial control spanning from Dhofar to the Hadhrami coast.
* 1395: The state is formally established by Badr as-Sahab ibn al-Habrali Bu Tuwairik, who consolidates tribal authority in the interior and designates Seiyun as the capital.
* 1414: Under the leadership of Sultan Ali bin Omar, the sultanate captures the Dhofar region with support from local religious elites.
* 1460s: The Kathiris conquer the strategic port of Ash-Shihr, significantly enhancing their maritime and economic standing.
* c. 1516–1565: The reign of Badr II ibn 'Abdallah (Badr Abu Tuwayriq), regarded as the most powerful Kathiri sultan. He modernizes the military using firearms and temporarily unifies nearly all of Hadhramaut.
* 16th Century: Abu Tuwayriq invites Yafa’i tribal mercenaries to assist in defending against northern Zaydi incursions. These tribes eventually settle on local estates, later evolving into autonomous rivals to Kathiri power.
* 1703: The Kasadi family, a group of Yafa'i origin, establishes an independent sultanate in Mukalla, marking the beginning of the loss of Kathiri coastal hegemony.
* c. 1730: The first state effectively collapses due to tribal fragmentation and pressure from Yafa’i and Qu'ayti forces, relapsing into a collection of autonomous local entities.
Second Kathiri State (1803–1858)
The second state represented a 19th-century revival of Kathiri centralized authority following nearly a century of political fragmentation.
* 1803: Sultan Jaafar bin Ali bin Omar returns to Hadhramaut from the diaspora in Java and India. He recruits military forces and builds alliances with religious elites to re-establish a unified Kathiri administration.
* Early 19th Century: The state focuses on internal stability and attempts to mitigate the tribal conflicts that had persisted since the fall of the first sultanate.
* 1858: The second state concludes following the rise of the Qu'ayti family. Sultan Mansur bin Omar is assassinated by the Qu'ayti Jamadar Awadh bin Muhammad, who subsequently seizes control of the vital town of Shibam.
Third Kathiri State (c. 1840s–1967)
Commonly known as the Kathiri State of Seiyun, the third state was defined by its rivalry with the Qu'ayti Sultanate and its eventual landlocked status under British protection.
* c. 1844: Sultan Ghalib bin Muhsin al-Kathiri utilizes a vast fortune earned as a commander in the Nizam of Hyderabad's army to purchase land and reclaim territory from Yafa’i strongmen.
* 1848: Seiyun is formally re-established as the permanent seat of the sultanate.
* 1873: Sultan al-Mansur ibn Ghalib commissions the construction of the Kathiri Palace in Seiyun, one of the world's largest mud-brick structures.
* 1888: The Kathiri state enters into formal treaty relations with Great Britain, though it initially maintains more autonomy than its Qu'ayti neighbors.
* 1918: The Aden Agreement is signed; the Kathiri sultan is forced to accept Qu'ayti suzerainty in exchange for formal British protection.
* 1939: Sultan Ja'far b. al-Mansur signs an advisory treaty with Britain, agreeing to the permanent presence of a British Resident Adviser.
* 1942–1946: The state asserts its administrative identity by issuing its own national postage stamps and silver coinage.
* October 2, 1967: During the South Arabian Revolution, the sultanate is overthrown by the National Liberation Front (NLF).
* November 30, 1967: The state is formally abolished and its territories incorporated into the independent People’s Republic of South Yemen.
